questions: If the start and end buildings are adjacent and the start floor Y_i equals the end floor Z_i, can the answer be zero (no stairs needed) because he can move directly via walkway without changing floors?
When moving between adjacent buildings via walkway, does the walkway connect only at the same floor number X, or can it connect at any floor up to the minimum height of the two buildings?

If a building has F_{i,j} floors, can Takahashi move via walkway from a floor X that is greater than F_{i,j} of the adjacent building? For example, from floor 5 in building A to floor 5 in building B if B only has 4 floors.
Are walkways bidirectional and always available between adjacent blocks, regardless of floor heights or other constraints?
Does moving up or down multiple floors in one building count as one stair use per floor changed, i.e., moving from floor 1 to 6 counts as 5 uses as given, but is moving from 6 to 1 also 5 uses?
Can Takahashi use stairs to go below floor 1 or above the top floor of a building? For example, if he is on floor 1, can he move down to a non-existent floor 0?
Is the goal to minimize only the number of stair uses, regardless of the number of walkway moves? Walkway moves have no cost, so they can be used arbitrarily?

If the start and end are in the same building but different floors, can he use walkways to other buildings and return to reduce stair uses? For example, go to an adjacent building at same floor via walkway, then use stairs there if cheaper, and return.
